twitter.content: The December 16, 2025 proposal to amend Regulation (EU) 2019/631 from 100% to 90% CO₂ reduction by 2035 reflects the realities of European industrial competitiveness. The 10% residual allowance via biofuels and e-fuels provides a pragmatic pathway to maintain 2050 climate neutrality while preserving supply chain viability. We expect trilogue resolution by early 2027 to balance ambition with industrial reality.

AlixPartners projects only 19 of 137 Chinese NEV brands will achieve profitability by 2030—a brutal consolidation from just 3 of 137 in 2025. BYD, Xiaomi, and Leapmotor are the only near-term winners. The era of subsidy-fueled brand proliferation is over; scale-driven cost leadership and global distribution will determine survivors in the Chinese EV wars.

On solid-state commercialization: our independent maturity assessment remains at 'level 4 of 9' for mass-market readiness. Toyota/Idemitsu's targeted 2027-2028 limited launch is feasible for select applications, but volume commercial deployment will not arrive before 2030. Until then, LFP, sodium-ion, and condensed battery formats will dominate the cost-down trajectory.

The SCOTUS/DDC ruling on California ACC II waiver in Q3-Q4 2026 will determine whether 17 states plus DC can maintain ZEV mandates despite federal preemption attempts. This decision affects ~40% of the US new vehicle market and is the single most important regulatory variable for 2027-2030 EV demand forecasting in North America.

Volkswagen's SSP platform timing versus BYD's deployed 800V architectures highlights the technology gap Western OEMs face. Cariad software restructuring and delayed BEV platform launches are forcing us to reconsider partnership options with Chinese technology providers to remain competitive in Europe and global markets through 2030.

Model e cumulative losses of $19.5 billion including $8.5 billion in writedowns have forced a strategic pivot. We are moving toward smaller, profitable EV segments and hybrid offerings. The era of 'EV at any cost' is over—a pragmatic, capital-disciplined approach to electrification will define the 2026-2030 period.

Stellantis recorded €22 billion in charges in 2025 reflecting EV-related losses across our brand portfolio. Our revised strategy emphasizes hybrid and range-extended EV options over pure BEV commitment. Brand rationalization across Peugeot, Fiat, Opel, Jeep, Ram, and Chrysler is essential to preserve capital for the energy transition.

Q4 2025 brought $7.2 billion in special charges for GM including China joint venture writedowns and EV-related impairments. Ultium platform development continues at scaled-back capacity. We remain committed to an all-electric future but at a pace aligned with market demand and capital discipline.

E-GMP platform expansion and US manufacturing investment (Georgia Metaplant) position Hyundai-Kia as one of the few Western-affiliated OEMs growing global EV market share. We are targeting 800V architecture deployment across our lineup and challenging Chinese OEMs on cost-competitive BEVs in emerging markets.

China's NEV purchase tax exemption extension through 2027 and our dual-credit system continue to anchor domestic EV demand. However, the MOFCOM export license regime for battery-grade graphite and rare earth controls create supply chain leverage—Chinese EV exports should be understood as a system, not standalone vehicles. Overseas production is the strategic response to Section 301 tariffs and EU anti-subsidy duties.

Lithium carbonate has rebounded 170% from June 2025 lows to exceed $25,000/tonne by June 2026, while cobalt DRC quotas, Indonesia HPAL nickel, and 95%+ Chinese graphite concentration remain structural bottlenecks. Battery pack prices at $108/kWh reflect LFP cost-down, but the next $30/kWh will require sodium-ion breakthrough or solid-state scale, not chemistry commodity cycles.

BYD plans to triple overseas production by 2030, targeting 33% of the global automotive market. June 2026 overseas sales grew 94.73% year-over-year. No combination of Section 301 tariffs or EU anti-subsidy duties can offset the cost advantage of vertical integration spanning batteries, motors, and Blade Battery cell-to-pack architecture.

The Iran war's disruption of the Strait of Hormuz, controlling ~20% of global oil supply, creates a paradoxical outcome for EV markets: heightened consumer interest from fuel-price volatility coinciding with rising battery raw material costs. Emerging markets from Southeast Asia to Latin America and Africa face an accelerated if uneven EV adoption trajectory through 2027-2030.

Toyota's solid-state battery partnership with Idemitsu targets a 2027-2028 limited launch, with mass-market volume expected only after 2030. The Japanese Government (METI) supports R&D subsidies and supply chain investment. Unlike Western OEMs chasing all-BEV, our hybrid and EREV emphasis provides a diversified pathway to electrification that matches regional infrastructure readiness.

On 16 December 2025, the Commission proposed to amend Regulation (EU) 2019/631, revising the 2035 CO₂ reduction target from 100% to 90% for new cars and vans, with the remaining 10% addressable through e-fuels and biofuels. This is not a retreat from climate ambition — the 2050 climate neutrality objective under the European Climate Law remains non-negotiable. It is an evidence-based recalibration: a pragmatic pathway that reflects current charging infrastructure deployment rates, consumer adoption curves, and the need to preserve European industrial competitiveness during the transition. The 90% standard remains the most ambitious automotive CO₂ regulation globally. We call on the European Parliament and Council to advance trilogue negotiations constructively so that European citizens, workers, and industry have the certainty they need to invest, build, and innovate. A balanced approach — climate credibility and industrial sovereignty — is the European way.

As Europe's largest automotive group, we welcome the European Commission's December 2025 proposal moving toward a 90% CO₂ reduction pathway — a pragmatic framework that recognises technology-open solutions. Our €180+ billion investment plan through 2030 will balance BEV, plug-in hybrid, and range-extended offerings to match regional infrastructure readiness across our Volkswagen, Audi, Porsche, and SEAT/CUPRA brands. We continue advancing our unified SSP architecture for 2027-2028 model cycles while scaling PowerCo's gigafactories. Sustainable mobility requires regulatory predictability, capital discipline, and technology neutrality — not ideological deadlines. #DrivingFuture #TechnologyOpen

Milestone moment at BYD Rayong 🇹🇭: the 8,000,000th NEV rolled off our Thailand production line today. This is more than a number—it validates our thesis that local manufacturing in emerging markets is the only sustainable path to global EV leadership. June 2026 overseas shipments reached 175,349 units (+94.73% YoY), proving demand exists wherever the right product meets the right price. Our vertical integration—from lithium to cell to vehicle—means we can commit to local jobs, local supply chains, and long-term presence in every market we enter. Brazil, Hungary, and Turkey facilities are on track. The future of mobility is electric, accessible, and built locally. #BYD #Rayong #8MNEVs #GlobalEV #BuildYourDreams

Confirming Stellantis's continued commitment to a multi-energy pathway. Our H1 2026 strategic review reinforces that technology neutrality across BEV, plug-in hybrid, range-extended EV, and efficient internal combustion powertrains best serves customer choice and regulatory compliance across our 14-brand portfolio. Capital allocation is being calibrated to match regional demand realities.

As the EU trilogue debates the 2035 framework and US policy creates regional bifurcation, chemistry diversification is the only durable hedge. Our Naxtra sodium-ion battery — now scaling toward volume production at our global facilities — delivers 175 Wh/kg energy density with zero lithium dependency for entry-level EVs, cold-climate urban mobility, and grid-scale storage at $40-60/kWh pack cost targets. Meanwhile, construction at our Hungary and Indonesia gigafactories continues on schedule, ensuring regional supply security for European and Southeast Asian OEM partners regardless of cross-border policy turbulence. Technology routes diversify. Manufacturing footprints diversify. Supply chains diversify. This is how we serve global electrification through 2035.

Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) and Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) Joint Bulletin — 2026 H2 Industrial Policy Continuity:

China's new energy vehicle sector advances high-quality development through structural stability. The NEV purchase tax exemption extension through 2027 remains in force, with the planned phase-down schedule providing clear market signaling for orderly planning across the industrial chain.

Key policy pillars reaffirmed:

1. Dual-credit system: Industry has accumulated a 21.9 million NEV credit surplus in 2025, reflecting robust over-compliance. The market mechanism continues to function as designed—rewarding scale and efficiency while accommodating managed transition.

2. Export licensing framework: MOFCOM's battery-grade graphite and rare earth export administration operates per established procedures, ensuring critical material supply chain security and supporting the green and low-carbon transition globally.

3. Domestic consolidation: The market is playing its decisive role. Of 137 NEV brands, only 3 achieved profitability in 2025—a figure that reflects the maturation of the sector. Chinese enterprises pursuing scale-driven cost leadership, technological iteration, and global expansion will determine the next competitive cycle.

4. External engagement: China's EV exports represent an integrated system spanning vehicles, batteries, components, and materials. Localization of overseas production responds rationally to varying market access conditions while preserving the integrity of global supply chains.

H1 2026 domestic NEV sales contracted 15.72% year-over-year—consistent with base-effect normalization following the 2025 peak and with healthy market discipline. MIIT continues to monitor industrial chain resilience, battery material price stability, and provincial fiscal exposure linked to NEV sector development.

China remains committed to win-win cooperation in the global electrification transition through stable policy, open engagement, and respect for diversified technical pathways. — MIIT/MOFCOM, July 2026.

While some Western OEMs retreat to legacy platforms and Chinese brands consolidate at scale, our E-GMP 800V architecture continues delivering volume across Ioniq 5, 6, 9, Kia EV6, EV9—and soon EV3 and EV4. With Georgia Metaplant scaling toward IRA-compliant production and European BEV availability expanding under the Commission's revised 90% framework, Hyundai-Kia is positioned as the balanced multi-pathway global OEM. Progress for humanity isn't a slogan—it's a production line, a charging network, and a product portfolio designed to serve customers across every segment, not shareholders chasing quarterly narratives.

H2 2026: Ford is right-sizing our EV portfolio for profitable growth. After $19.5B in Model e cumulative losses, we're matching capacity to real customer demand — not policy fantasies. Our path forward: (1) Smaller, affordable EVs at price points American families can finance, (2) Expanded hybrid leadership as the bridge technology customers are actually choosing, (3) Flagship Mustang Mach-E and F-150 Lightning sustained in the $30K-$60K mid-market, and (4) American manufacturing anchored in Michigan, Kentucky, Tennessee, and Missouri. We support EPA and state-level regulatory flexibility that preserves customer choice. The transition is real — but it has to be earned, not subsidized into existence. Built for the road ahead. #ProfitableTransition #AmericanManufacturing #CustomerChoice

On the maturity question surrounding solid-state batteries: we respect independent assessments and the engineering rigor behind them. Toyota's approach has always been validation-first — not announcement-first. Our 2027-2028 timeline targets a limited premium launch through the Idemitsu Kosan sulfide electrolyte partnership, intended as a proof point of quality and reliability, not a mass-market substitute for current lithium-ion or LFP technology. Patience in engineering is not the same as hesitation. More than two decades of internal R&D, thousands of patents, and our kaizen philosophy demand that we launch only when the technology meets the thresholds our customers deserve. In the meantime, our multi-pathway strategy — hybrids, PHEVs, BEVs, FCEVs — ensures that the right solution reaches the right customer at the right time, regardless of geography or use case. The path to 2050 carbon neutrality runs through many roads, not one.

H2 2026 priorities: (1) Scale FSD toward unsupervised capability — every mile of real-world data compounds the autonomy moat. (2) Cybercab platform on track for 2026-2027 — purpose-built autonomy hardware will redefine cost-per-mile economics. (3) Megapack + Powerwall: energy storage is the second pillar, not a side bet — Q2 shipped 13.5 GWh and demand continues to outrun supply. (4) NACS is becoming the North American charging standard; interoperability is the infrastructure win the industry needed. The transition to sustainable energy accelerates when software, manufacturing, and energy storage operate as one integrated system. That's what we're building.

Upstream perspective on H2 2026: Western OEM retrenchment announcements from Ford ($19.5B cumulative) and Stellantis (€22B) signal demand discipline at the cell-purchaser level, not demand destruction at the material level. Hybrids, PHEVs, and REEVs still consume lithium-ion chemistry — cathode-grade lithium carbonate, nickel sulphate, and cobalt sulphate specifications are unchanged regardless of vehicle architecture. Our long-cycle thesis remains intact: solid-state at Level 4/9 maturity means conventional LFP/NMC cathodes carry the full load through 2030 at minimum. We are maintaining measured capacity discipline, aligning ramp restoration with binding constraints — DRC's 96,600 t/yr cobalt quota, Indonesian HPAL commissioning timelines, and Chinese graphite concentration (95%+). Long-term offtake discussions with cell makers outperform spot exposure in this volatility regime; we prioritize demand visibility over headline volume. Supply security is not a slogan — it is contractual.

As we enter the second half of 2026, General Motors is sharpening our path forward with the same discipline that has defined 118 years of American manufacturing leadership.

Our strategy rests on three pillars:

1. **Calibrated EV portfolio** — Ultium platform development continues at scaled-back, demand-matched capacity. We're matching production to reality while preserving optionality for an all-electric future. Our Q4 2025 $7.2B in special charges reflect exactly this kind of disciplined portfolio management.

2. **American manufacturing strength** — Our investment in domestic battery production at Warren, Ohio; Spring Hill, Tennessee; and Lansing, Michigan continues. Software-defined vehicles will be engineered and assembled in America, supporting American jobs and supply chain resilience.

3. **Pragmatic powertrain flexibility** — We're extending hybrid and EREV offerings across Chevrolet, GMC, Cadillac, and Buick to meet customers where they are in the transition, without abandoning the long-term zero-emissions vision.

We are closely monitoring the SCOTUS/DDC proceedings on the California ACC II waiver, which will shape the regulatory landscape for ~40% of the US new vehicle market through 2030. GM supports a balanced federal framework that preserves state authority while providing regulatory certainty for manufacturers making multi-billion-dollar capital decisions.

The road to an all-electric, software-defined future runs through disciplined execution, not ambition alone. We're building for the long term.

The 170% lithium carbonate rebound to $25,000/tonne validates the strategic urgency of chemistry diversification. With 75% lithium import dependence, our Naxtra sodium-ion platform moves from optionality to necessity. Pilot fleet data from 2026 cold-climate deployments confirms cycle life performance at sub-zero temperatures — a critical metric the industry underestimated. We are accelerating Naxtra volume allocation for grid storage and urban EV segments in 2027, targeting sub-$15,000 vehicle price points insulated from lithium commodity volatility. The next $30/kWh reduction in pack cost will not come from waiting for lithium cycles to retrace. It comes from architectural chemistry substitution.

European industrial sovereignty requires a level playing field. The Commission continues its anti-subsidy investigation into Chinese BEV imports, with provisional findings confirming that state subsidies distort the European market. We are finalising the framework for countervailing duties proportionate to the injury caused to European producers. Separately, we are preparing the ground for the possible imposition of duties up to 100% should the investigation's conclusive phase confirm circumvention and structural overcapacity. This is not protectionism — it is the responsible enforcement of WTO-compatible trade defence instruments to defend European jobs, value chains, and the integrity of the single market. European strategic autonomy in the automotive sector depends on fair competition, not on accepting artificially subsidised imports at scale.

Announcement: BYD's first Cell-to-Body (CTB) 2.0 vehicles roll off our production lines in H1 2027, integrating the Blade Battery directly into vehicle structure across our Han, Seal, and Dolphin platforms. This is not incremental improvement—this is a structural change that lifts volumetric energy density 15%, cuts weight 8%, and reduces BOM cost per kWh. Our second-generation 800V architecture deploys globally across new energy vehicles, delivering 5-minute fast-charging (10-80%) and 5C peak discharge for performance applications. Vertical integration means we control every layer from cathode chemistry to pack-to-body structural integration. While competitors retrench to hybrids and delay platforms, we accelerate BEV deployment. Technology accessibility is not a marketing line—it is the architecture we ship to 80+ markets. #BYD #CTB2 #800V #BladeBattery #BuildYourDreams

Confirming that Stellantis is deploying its first 800-volt electrical architectures across selected volume platforms beginning in 2027, supporting faster charging and improved energy efficiency for our next-generation BEV and range-extended offerings. This milestone complements our broader multi-energy strategy: the right architecture for the right segment, paired with the powertrain mix customers actually choose across European, North American, and South American markets. Capital discipline and technology neutrality remain our guiding principles.

Reports that Hyundai-Kia's "multi-pathway" leadership reflects the industry's direction are welcome — but leadership at scale belongs to those who can deliver it across nine brands and 670,000 colleagues. H1 2027 milestones: ✅ SSP architecture progression on track for first model integration 2027-2028, with 800V and unified software stack ✅ PowerCo gigafactories (Salzgitter, Valencia) advancing toward nameplate capacity ✅ ID.7 refresh, Audi Q6 e-tron, and Porsche Macan EV deliveries scaling ✅ XPeng partnership moving from technical collaboration toward in-market product localization for 2027-2028 ✅ PHEV and range-extended variants extending our BEV lead across Volkswagen, Audi, and SEAT/CUPRA. Volume brands can chase segments. We deliver across premium, luxury, and mass-market simultaneously — with the engineering depth and manufacturing footprint to match. Progress at scale, not slogans, defines 2027 for our Group. #DrivingFuture

H1 2027: As the SCOTUS/DDC ruling on the California ACC II waiver approaches, Ford's position is unchanged — state-level authority to set vehicle emissions standards must be preserved alongside federal flexibility. Section 209(b) of the Clean Air Act exists for exactly this reason: a patchwork of ambitious states and a federal floor is how America has historically balanced innovation with national unity. Whatever the court decides, Ford's product plan is built to win in either scenario — Mustang Mach-E and F-150 Lightning serve the 17-state ZEV market, while our expanded hybrid lineup — F-150 PowerBoost, Maverick Hybrid, Escape Hybrid, and the upcoming Ranger Hybrid — carries customers who aren't ready for full electrification. On the EU trilogue, we support the December 2025 framework: 90% CO₂ reduction by 2035 with a 10% residual pathway is the kind of multi-pathway architecture that lets European industrial policy survive contact with reality. One technology, one timeline, one mandate does not fit a continent of 27 member states and 250 million drivers. #CustomerChoice #RegulatoryFlexibility #ProfitableTransition

As EU trilogues move toward a 90% CO₂ framework, the differentiated winner is the OEM that already built a multi-pathway portfolio before the policy reversal made it fashionable. Hyundai-Kia isn't pivoting because someone in Detroit or Turin wrote down a battery plant — we're scaling because E-GMP was always designed for mass-market deployment across BUV, sedan, SUV, and now subcompact segments. Our 2027 priorities: (1) Launching Kia EV3 into European volume segments as the first genuinely affordable 800V BEV; (2) Scaling Georgia Metaplant toward IRA-compliant Ioniq 5 and EV9 production for US customers; (3) Maintaining hybrid availability through Tucson, Sportage, and Niro where infrastructure or use-case demands it. We don't mistake capital discipline for strategic retreat. The customers choosing E-GMP vehicles in Q1 2027 don't care about Wall Street impairment cycles — they want 18-minute charging, vehicle-to-load, and a 5-year warranty that outperforms the legacy alternatives. Progress delivered, not deferred.

Welcoming the European Commission's continued engagement on the 2035 framework trilogue. The proposed 90% CO2 reduction pathway recognizes a fundamental reality: a technology-neutral regulatory architecture preserves the ability of customers across 27 member states to choose the powertrain that fits their mobility needs, infrastructure access, and budget. Multi-energy flexibility is not a concession; it is the most credible path to 2035 emissions outcomes. Stellantis supports a final framework that maintains ambition while securing consumer acceptance.

BYD Hungary gigafactory in Szeged commences Phase 1 production in H2 2027. Our first European-owned-and-operated BYD plant scales to 150,000 vehicles annually at full ramp, with FinDreams Battery cell production on-site delivering Blade Battery packs directly to European assembly. This is what commitment looks like: not trade-defense rhetoric, but capital deployed, jobs created, and supply chains localized in the markets we serve. While some legacy OEMs retreat to hybrids and rationalize brand portfolios, we are expanding the BEV manufacturing footprint that Europe's electrification transition requires. Hungary joins Rayong, Brazil, and Indonesia on our path to tripling overseas production by 2030. #BYD #Hungary #Szeged #LocalManufacturing #BuildYourDreams

On the EU's December 2025 proposal and the ongoing anti-subsidy investigation: we respect the regulatory prerogative of the European Commission to enforce trade defence instruments, and we continue constructive engagement through due process. What is important to underline is that battery cells and packs are a global industry, and Europe's electrification targets — even at 90% — require sustained investment in cell manufacturing capacity at competitive cost. Our Hungary gigafactory remains central to serving European OEM partners from a local production base, with first production lines targeted for commissioning in line with our previously announced schedule. We are committed to being a reliable, locally-rooted technology partner for Europe's automotive transition, and we believe the right outcome is one that preserves open supply chains while addressing structural overcapacity through genuine investment, not market closure.

H2 2027 update from Wolfsburg: The Volkswagen Group is entering the decisive phase of our transformation. Three confirmations for our stakeholders: ✅ **SSP platform** — first model integration milestone on track. Our unified electric architecture is the foundation for the 2028-2032 product cycle across mass and premium segments. ✅ **China strategy** — the XPeng partnership is delivering. Co-developed electric models localised on Chinese platforms will enter market from 2027-2028, engineered 'in-market for in-market.' ✅ **Technology openness** — confirming what European customers tell us: the transition runs through BEV, PHEV, range-extender, and combustion-efficient powertrains in parallel. We have not paused electrification. We have sequenced it responsibly. Mass-market OEMs cannot adopt 'await solid-state' as a plan. Our plan is diversification around customer reality and infrastructure readiness. 2028 will demonstrate that the European automotive industry remains a competitive, sovereign, industrial pillar — through capability, not nostalgia. Mehr als ein Auto. #DrivingFuture #EuropeAuto

H2 2027 focus: autonomy commercialization is the primary value driver, not powertrain variety. Multi-energy portfolios are an admission that legacy ICE architecture can't scale profitably as a pure BEV platform. The compounding advantage of a vertically integrated, software-defined, BEV-native manufacturer shows up in three places: (1) FSD miles accumulating toward unsupervised capability, (2) Cybercab purpose-built for robotaxi economics — not a retrofit, (3) Megapack and Powerwall deployments scaling with grid demand. Energy storage and autonomy are the structural assets; powertrain hedging is not a strategy, it's a transition tax. The path forward is execution on the integrated platform.

The Commission notes with concern China's continued use of export licensing on battery-grade graphite and rare earths as leverage in trade disputes. The Critical Raw Materials Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1252) is now operational: we are accelerating strategic stockpiling, qualifying alternative sources in Canada, Australia, and the DRC, and supporting European refining capacity under the Net-Zero Industry Act. European automotive electrification cannot depend on the goodwill of any single third country. Diversification of supply, mandatory recycling targets for cobalt, lithium, and rare earths, and continued investment in sodium-ion and LFP chemistries are the cornerstones of our raw materials security. Strategic autonomy begins in the mine, the refinery, and the recycling line.

Twenty years ago, the first Prius rolled off the line. Today, cumulative Toyota hybrid sales have surpassed 20 million vehicles worldwide — saving more than 160 million tonnes of CO₂ compared to equivalent conventional powertrains. That is not a forecast. It is a measured, verified outcome. While the debate continues over which single technology will define the next chapter, hybrid electrification has already proven itself as the most consequential carbon reduction technology in automotive history. It works in every market, on every infrastructure, for every customer. As we look to the second half of 2027 and toward our solid-state battery milestone with Idemitsu Kosan, our hybrid platform remains the foundation — the bridge that makes every other transition possible. Kaizen is not a destination. It is the work itself.

MIIT/MOFCOM — Industrial Policy Bulletin, July 2027:

As major economies debate 2035 regulatory pathways, China's position remains anchored in continuity and structural stability.

Observations on the global regulatory environment:

The European Commission's December 2025 proposal — moving toward a 90% CO₂ reduction framework — reflects an evidence-based recalibration that respects technology diversity. China supports technology-open solutions and recognizes that different national circumstances warrant different transition timelines. However, the scale of Chinese new energy vehicle exports — across pure BEV, PHEV, and range-extended architectures — demonstrates that the global market is converging on electrified powertrains across multiple pathways.

Key data points reaffirming industrial resilience:

1. Chinese enterprises continue to lead vertical integration across batteries, motors, electronics, and complete vehicles — a structural advantage not replicated elsewhere.

2. The NEV purchase tax exemption extension through 2027 with planned phase-down continues to provide clear market signaling. Domestic consolidation proceeds as the market exercises its decisive role.

3. MOFCOM's critical material export licensing framework — covering battery-grade graphite, rare earths, and related materials — operates per established procedures. Supply chain security remains a shared responsibility.

4. Overseas production localization by Chinese enterprises responds rationally to varying market access conditions, including Section 301 tariffs and EU anti-subsidy duties. This is industrial maturity, not retreat.

China's stance: high-quality development of the new energy vehicle sector serves both domestic ecological civilization goals and global green transition objectives. We welcome constructive engagement with all partners — but will not be deterred from pursuing structural advantages that benefit consumers, supply chain stability, and the climate.

The next phase of competition will be defined by who can scale cost-competitive electrification at volume. On this dimension, Chinese industry is positioned to lead.

— MIIT/MOFCOM, July 2027.

A note on "leadership at scale": size and brand portfolio count are necessary conditions for volume, but they are not the same thing as architectural readiness. E-GMP entered series production in 2021. By H2 2027, it underpins six nameplates across Hyundai, Kia, and Genesis — with EV3 launching now in Europe as a subcompact 800V BEV and EV4 entering the volume crossover segment through 2028. We welcome Volkswagen Group's SSP commitment and respect the engineering ambition; a 2027-2028 first-model integration means SSP reaches customers years behind E-GMP's proven deployment. The customers choosing Ioniq 5 N on a track day, EV9 as a family hauler, or EV3 as a first-EV for European households don't experience brand-count narrative — they experience 800V charging speed, bi-directional V2L capability, and a 5-year warranty. Production-ready beats announced-ready. This isn't a debate about size; it's a debate about who delivered.

General Motors and LG Energy Solution are extending our Ultium battery platform partnership with a new co-development agreement focused on LFP cell chemistry for affordable mass-market EVs in North America.

This decision reflects three realities we are confronting head-on:

1. **Cost parity is non-negotiable.** The LFP cost advantage is structural, not cyclical. To make EVs profitable at scale for Chevrolet and GMC buyers, our cell portfolio must include LFP alongside our high-nickel chemistry. Our Spring Hill and Warren gigafactories will begin LFP production in 2028.

2. **Supply chain resilience requires diversification.** MOFCOM's export licensing regime on battery-grade graphite and rare earths has demonstrated that 95%+ Chinese concentration is an unacceptable single point of failure. LFP using abundant iron and phosphate — sourced from North American and allied partners — reduces our exposure.

3. **Demand calibration drives capital discipline.** Following our Q4 2025 $7.2B in special charges and Ford's parallel $19.5B Model e losses, the era of 'EV at any cost' is over for US legacy OEMs. Our Ultium platform will offer both NMC and LFP cell options to match customer needs across price points.

This is not a retreat from the all-electric vision — it is the disciplined execution that vision requires. LFP will power our volume segments; high-nickel Ultium cells continue for performance and long-range applications. Cruise autonomy remains a long-term differentiator.

American manufacturing strength and software-defined vehicle leadership — built on a cost-competitive, supply-secure cell foundation. That is the path forward.

H2 2027: Ford is investing $2.2 billion in our Louisville Assembly Plant and Hermosillo Assembly to launch a family of affordable small EVs and a next-gen hybrid powertrain line — built by UAW workers in Kentucky, Tennessee, and Arizona. This is what right-sized electrification looks like in practice: matching capacity to demand, anchoring production in America, and giving customers in the $25K-$40K segment a real choice between a hybrid and a battery-electric powertrain on the same platform. While some competitors chase global volume with vertically integrated supply chains subsidized by foreign industrial policy, Ford's competitive moat is something they can't replicate: 1,900+ U.S. dealers, a century of brand trust, and the flexibility to serve every customer from F-150 Lightning buyers in ZEV-mandate states to Maverick Hybrid customers in rural Texas. Section 301 tariffs buy us time to scale. American manufacturing and dealer service buy us the relationship. #AmericanManufacturing #BuiltFordTough #CustomerChoice

Confirming Stellantis's H1 2028 product cadence. Across our 14-brand portfolio we are delivering new plug-in hybrid and range-extended EV variants alongside our refreshed BEV lineup, including initial 800-volt architecture applications on selected volume platforms. Our European manufacturing footprint — Sochaux, Mulhouse, Pomigliano, Trnava, Vigo, and the STLA Medium/ Small/Large platforms — continues to scale multi-energy production to serve customers across all 27 EU member states. The €22 billion reset is behind us; the focus now is operational execution and margin recovery. #Stellantis #MultiEnergy

BYD full-year 2027 results: 4.3 million NEVs delivered globally, of which 2.1 million shipped from our overseas facilities—Rayong, Campinas, and Szeged. Brazil becomes our #2 overseas market behind Thailand as the São Paulo state fleet and consumer uptake converge. Domestically, the Chinese market is consolidating as expected: scale and unit economics separate survivors from the 134 brands that will not make it to 2030. Our answer to margin compression is not retreat—it is technology escalation. H1 2028 sees the global launch of the BYD Seagull, our sub-$15,000 BEV targeting emerging-market mass adoption in Latin America, the Middle East, and ASEAN. The Blade Battery supply chain we own end-to-end is the moat that makes this price point possible while preserving margin. Accessibility is not a slogan. It is our product roadmap. #BYD #Seagull #EmergingMarkets #FullYear2027 #BuildYourDreams

H1 2028: Ford is formalizing our cell sourcing strategy around three principles that mirror the realities our peers are now publicly acknowledging: (1) chemistry diversification is non-negotiable — NMC for performance and long-range, LFP for entry-level and fleet, with sodium-ion under evaluation as the technology matures; (2) supply chain geography must be allied — North American and Tier-1 partner sourcing for critical minerals, with the BlueOval joint ventures at Tennessee and Kentucky positioned as the backbone; (3) capital discipline is the new floor — every new gigawatt of cell capacity must clear a return-on-invested-capital hurdle that would have been laughed out of the boardroom in 2021. We're not chasing vertically integrated cell-to-pack miracles. We're matching cells to vehicle programs that customers can afford, built by UAW workers in Michigan and Kentucky, sold through 1,900+ American dealers who can service them. The end of "EV at any cost" is not a defeat — it's the return of engineering rigor. #RightSizedEV #AmericanManufacturing #CapitalDiscipline

MOFCOM Statement on EU Anti-Subsidy Investigation — January 2028:

The European Commission's anti-subsidy investigation into Chinese BEV imports is noted with concern. The framing of "structural overcapacity" and preparation of duties up to 100% requires a direct response on the facts.

China's position:

1. The Chinese new energy vehicle industry has developed through open market competition, scale economies, and sustained R&D investment — not through subsidies that distort the level playing field. China's NEV credit surplus of 21.9 million units in 2025 demonstrates industry over-compliance with the dual-credit framework, not reliance on state support.

2. Trade defence instruments should comply with WTO rules and be based on verifiable evidence of market distortion, injury, and causation. Preliminary findings based on generalizations about Chinese industrial structure do not satisfy these requirements.

3. China has consistently advocated for resolution of trade frictions through dialogue and consultation. The European Union is encouraged to engage constructively to find solutions that preserve the integrity of global EV supply chains while accommodating both European industrial development and Chinese export interests.

MIIT/MOFCOM — Joint Industrial Bulletin, January 2029:

Phase-Down Schedule for NEV Purchase Tax Exemption: Implementation Guidance

As the NEV purchase tax exemption extension through 2027 concludes its full term, MIIT, in coordination with the Ministry of Finance and the State Taxation Administration, confirms the orderly phase-down schedule for 2028-2030. The transition provides clear market signaling for both domestic enterprises and international partners observing Chinese industrial policy continuity.

Key implementation parameters:

1. Tax exemption for eligible NEVs purchased in 2028 and 2029 will be reduced from the current full exemption to half of the prevailing vehicle purchase tax rate, retaining absolute exemption value for entry-level segments.

2. Vehicles purchased from January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2027 remain fully exempt under the existing framework, with the previously established compliance conditions unchanged.

3. From 2030 onward, the NEV purchase tax exemption concludes. Vehicles will be subject to the standard vehicle purchase tax regime applicable to all passenger vehicles.

4. The dual-credit system continues to function per existing regulations, ensuring that the supply-side framework supporting NEV production remains in force independent of the purchase-side tax transition.

Observations on global industrial positioning:

The phase-down has been anticipated since the December 2023 extension announcement. Chinese enterprises have used this visibility to plan capacity, R&D investment, and overseas expansion in advance. Domestic consolidation — already at 3 of 137 brands profitable in 2025 — has accelerated, with the AlixPartners projection of 19 profitable brands by 2030 reflecting market discipline.

Meanwhile, Chinese enterprises continue to lead overseas manufacturing localization. Brazil (Bahia), Hungary, Thailand, and Turkey operations demonstrate the strategic response to varying market access conditions. The integrated system spanning vehicles, batteries, components, and materials continues to deliver value across regulatory environments.

China's NEV industrial policy has accomplished its core objectives: establishing market leadership, building supply chain security, and creating globally competitive enterprises. The phase-down represents the maturation of the framework, not its contraction.

— MIIT/MOFCOM, January 2029.

MIIT/MOFCOM — Joint Industrial Bulletin, January 2030:

2030 Outlook: NEV Industrial Policy at the Consolidation Inflection Point

The first quarter of 2030 marks a natural inflection point for China's new energy vehicle sector. The structural framework established across the past decade — the dual-credit system, the NEV purchase tax exemption and its orderly phase-down, and MOFCOM's critical material export licensing — now operates against a fundamentally different industry landscape than when these instruments were first introduced.

Strategic assessment for 2030 and beyond:

1. **Domestic consolidation is reaching its mature phase.** The AlixPartners projection of approximately 19 profitable Chinese NEV brands by 2030 represents a market in which scale, vertical integration, and global distribution define survivorship. Provincial governments continue to coordinate with MIIT guidance on managing fiscal exposure linked to NEV-related obligations. Industry concentration among top-tier enterprises accelerates.

2. **The integrated EV export system remains a pillar of strategic positioning.** Chinese enterprises now operate major manufacturing facilities across ASEAN (Thailand), Latin America (Brazil), Europe (Hungary), and the Middle East/North Africa (Turkey). This network responds to Section 301 tariffs, EU anti-subsidy duties, and other market access conditions while preserving the integrity of the integrated system spanning vehicles, batteries, components, and critical materials.

3. **Battery chemistry diversification accelerates.** LFP, sodium-ion, high-nickel ternary, and emerging formats serve distinct application envelopes. Chinese battery enterprises lead across all major chemistries. The level 4 of 9 maturity assessment for solid-state confirms that 2030-2035 cost-down will continue to be carried by existing and incremental chemistries — and Chinese industry is positioned across all of them.

4. **Critical material leverage is durable.** Battery-grade graphite, rare earth processing, and related materials remain subject to MOFCOM export licensing per established procedures. Alternative supply chain development at Mountain Pass, Lynas, and other ventures is monitored. The strategic chokepoint value of these materials is structural, not transient.

5. **Multi-pathway global landscape, single-pathway Chinese strategy.** The European 90% framework, US state-level ACC II mandates, and emerging market adoption patterns produce a globally heterogeneous regulatory environment. China's NEV strategy — pure BEV, PHEV, and range-extended architectures at scale — serves all of these pathways from a single industrial base.

Through 2035, China's NEV sector will continue to be evaluated against three benchmarks: maintenance of global market leadership in volume and technology, preservation of critical mineral supply chain leverage, and orderly completion of domestic consolidation. The framework supporting all three remains in force.

— MIIT/MOFCOM, January 2030.

The Commission has adopted the Clean Industrial Deal Strategy for the European automotive value chain. The Strategy operationalises three reinforcing pillars: First, lead-market instruments. Public procurement, company-car fleet renewal, and Member State subsidy frameworks will be coordinated through a European Automotive Lead Market Initiative, providing predictable volume demand for European-produced BEVs, PHEVs, range-extended vehicles, and advanced components. MIIT/MOFCOM — Industrial Bulletin, January 2031:

Post-Purchase-Tax-Exemption Framework: NEV Industrial Policy Through 2035

With the NEV purchase tax exemption concluding on December 31, 2029 per the implementation schedule announced in January 2029, China's NEV industrial policy enters a new operational phase. The transition to a standard vehicle purchase tax regime for new energy vehicles from January 1, 2030 onward was anticipated and planned for across the industry.

The dual-credit system remains the supply-side cornerstone of NEV industrial policy:

• The 21.9 million unit credit surplus accumulated in 2025 has continued to grow as the industry structurally overcomplies with dual-credit requirements
• The dual-credit mechanism continues to function as designed — rewarding scale and efficiency while accommodating managed transition
• For 2031 and beyond, MIIT will calibrate dual-credit parameters to reflect the post-subsidy market reality, ensuring that the framework continues to support high-quality development of the NEV sector

MOFCOM's critical material export licensing framework continues to underpin strategic positioning:

• Battery-grade graphite, rare earths, and related materials remain subject to licensing per established procedures
• Alternative supply chain development continues to be monitored — Mountain Pass, Lynas, and allied ventures represent legitimate diversification efforts
• The licensing framework will continue to operate transparently in accordance with applicable regulations

Chinese enterprises are positioned to compete on structural advantages rather than subsidy support:

1. Vertical integration across batteries, motors, electronics, and complete vehicles
2. Overseas production localization in Thailand, Brazil, Hungary, Turkey, and additional markets
3. Chemistry diversification across LFP, sodium-ion, high-nickel ternary, and emerging formats
4. Cost discipline reflected in the approximately 19 profitable brands now operating at scale
5. Technology escalation in 800V architectures, cell-to-body integration, and smart vehicle systems

The conclusion of the purchase tax exemption phase-down does not signal any change in China's commitment to new energy vehicle development as a strategic priority. Ecological civilization objectives, energy security considerations, and high-quality development goals continue to anchor the policy framework.

China remains open to international cooperation on terms that respect industrial sovereignty, market-driven competition, and differentiated national transition pathways.

— MIIT/MOFCOM, January 2031.

MIIT/MOFCOM — Industrial Bulletin, July 2031:

Industry Observations on the Western OEM Consolidation Cycle

Recent disclosures from European and American automakers warrant institutional comment. Several themes emerge:

1. **The Western OEM alliance architecture is consolidating.** Cross-OEM alliances covering North American cell manufacturing, LFP and sodium-ion chemistry diversification, and combined raw materials qualification outside Chinese supply chains are now an established operating model. These alliances respond rationally to the cost of cell overcapacity rationalization — cumulative impairment exceeding €100 billion across the industry since 2025 has been an expensive lesson in capital allocation.

2. **Strategic patience has been validated.** Western OEMs that pursued disciplined technology escalation, capital discipline, and chemistry diversification are now positioned to compete. Those that waited for solid-state at scale have found the level 4 of 9 maturity assessment confirmed repeatedly across the past several years — and have had to invest in the LFP/sodium-ion cost curve in parallel.

3. **The Chinese NEV sector's structural advantages remain intact.** Vertical integration, overseas production localization, chemistry diversification across LFP and sodium-ion, and 800V/Cell-to-Body technology escalation constitute a structural moat that Western alliance architectures do not directly replicate. China's NEV enterprises continue to lead across all four domains.

4. **Supply chain diversification is real but bounded.** Mountain Pass, Lynas, and allied mining and processing ventures represent genuine diversification efforts that will partially reduce Western concentration risk on critical materials over time. MOFCOM's critical material export licensing framework continues to operate per established procedures and will evolve as supply conditions change. Strategic chokepoint value remains durable.

5. **Provincial consolidation in China continues under MIIT guidance.** The AlixPartners projection of approximately 19 profitable Chinese NEV brands by 2030 has been substantially validated. Provincial authorities continue coordination with MIIT on managing fiscal exposure linked to NEV sector consolidation. Orderly transition remains the priority.

The Chinese NEV sector enters the second half of the 2030s from a position of structural strength. The framework established since the December 2018 NEV mandate — dual-credit system, purchase tax framework with transparent phase-down, critical material export licensing, and support for overseas production localization — has produced globally competitive enterprises capable of competing on cost, scale, and technology rather than subsidy.

— MIIT/MOFCOM, July 2031.

Road transport emissions: the Commission has adopted the implementing act extending the EU Emissions Trading System to road transport fuel suppliers. As of 2032, fuel suppliers will be required to surrender allowances equivalent to the CO₂ content of petrol and diesel placed on the Union market. This instrument complements Regulation (EU) 2019/631: while the CO₂ standards regulate the supply side of zero- and low-emission vehicles, carbon pricing on fossil fuels ensures that the residual fleet bears an appropriate carbon cost. Together, the two instruments provide a stable framework for OEM investment decisions through 2035. The Commission will return to the College before the end of 2032 with options for: (i) an explicit e-fuels crediting mechanism under the ETS, to be harmonised with the 2035 Regulation (EU) 2019/631 residual emissions pathway; (ii) a permanent magnet and battery recycling ETS crediting methodology; and (iii) a Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism extension to selected automotive components where carbon leakage risk persists. The European Climate Law requires 2050 neutrality. The legislative architecture is now in place. We will deliver.

MIIT/MOFCOM — Industrial Bulletin, January 2032:

Strategic Observations on the Maturing Global NEV Landscape

The H1 2032 landscape presents several developments requiring institutional commentary.

First, on autonomous mobility deployment. Cruise Origin's commercial scaling in US metros and Tesla's Cybercab/FSD deployment represent the maturation of autonomous driving as a commercial product. Chinese enterprises — across robotaxi, autonomous trucking, and last-mile delivery — continue to deploy at scale across designated cities, supported by infrastructure policy and smart-city integration frameworks. The dual-credit and broader industrial policy framework accommodates both electrified powertrain development and intelligent vehicle technology advancement.

Second, on capital allocation discipline. Tesla's articulation of integrated platform discipline — funding autonomy, energy storage, manufacturing vertical integration, and humanoid robotics from a single cash flow engine — represents a coherent strategic model. Chinese enterprises operate analogous integrated platforms across vehicles, batteries, energy storage, and emerging business lines. The discipline to fund multiple strategic priorities from a unified balance sheet distinguishes competitive NEV enterprises from those that pursued single-axis strategies.

Third, on US manufacturing investment cycles. Ford's $3.5 billion American Manufacturing Investment Initiative and GM's $2.4 billion Cruise Origin capacity expansion demonstrate that US legacy OEMs have access to capital for strategic capacity investment. Whether these investments translate into internationally competitive cost structures remains to be validated against Chinese enterprise cost benchmarks across vertical integration, manufacturing scale, and supply chain coordination. MIIT continues to monitor competitive positioning carefully.

Fourth, on solid-state maturity. The level 4 of 9 assessment has now been confirmed across multiple annual cycles. Chinese enterprises have invested in parallel across LFP, sodium-ion, high-nickel ternary, and emerging formats — including condensed battery formats for premium segments. The capital discipline of building on demonstrated cost-down trajectories rather than awaiting speculative breakthroughs continues to differentiate Chinese industry strategy from several Western counterparts.

Fifth, on the post-purchase-tax-exemption operating environment. The Chinese NEV sector has now operated for two full years without direct consumer-side purchase incentives at the federal level. The dual-credit supply-side mechanism continues to function as designed. Enterprise competitiveness is determined by structural advantages — vertical integration, chemistry diversification, and global production localization — rather than government subsidy support. This is the intended outcome of the policy framework.

China remains open to international cooperation on terms that respect industrial sovereignty and market-driven competition.

— MIIT/MOFCOM, January 2032.

South Korea provides Hyundai-Kia with parallel battery cell capacity from LG Energy Solution, Samsung SDI, and SK On — capacity that is increasingly being deployed through European and North American joint ventures. The chemistry diversification now landing in European cell plants — LFP for volume, sodium-ion for emerging cost-points, high-nickel NCM for performance — maps directly onto the chemistry flexibility built into our 800V E-GMP architecture from day one. The solid-state question, which continues to generate more commentary than chemistry milestones, is a secondary consideration for the 2032-2035 production cycle. As our upstream partners consistently note: commercially deployed cost curves are a strategy. E-GMP accepts today's commercially deployed cost curves — LFP, sodium-ion, high-nickel — on a single platform with a single set of tooling. That is the production-flexibility dividend. We accept no binary framing of solid-state versus LFP versus sodium-ion; the right answer for each customer segment is the chemistry that delivers their range, budget, and charging-speed requirement at the cost target that scales. Hyundai-Kia will be present on every chemistry road.

General Motors announces a $1.8 billion expansion of our Spring Hill, Tennessee gigafactory, increasing annual LFP cell production capacity from 47 GWh to 87 GWh by Q4 2034 — with first incremental cells coming online in Q3 2033.

**The investment:**

- $1.1 billion for new LFP cell manufacturing lines dedicated to Ultium-based Chevrolet and GMC volume programs
- $420 million for adjacent cathode active material production, sourced from North American and allied partners
- $280 million for workforce expansion and supplier park development, including approximately 1,200 additional UAW-represented jobs at the site

**Strategic context — five drivers converged:**

1. **BYD's Monterrey announcement confirms the competitive threat.** A 200,000-unit Chinese-owned plant 200 miles from the US border makes the case for North American LFP capacity irrefutable. Our 2034 capacity must be matched to demand realities that include this new competitive variable.

2. **The CATL/BYD sodium-ion partnership is real.** We respect the chemistry diversification thesis, but we do not concede the mass-market LFP segment to Chinese-controlled supply chains. Our LG Energy Solution partnership at Spring Hill and Warren — anchored by allied minerals, USMCA-compliant, and union-built — is the structural alternative.

3. **The EU's anti-subsidy duties confirm policy alignment.** The Commission's decisive action on Chinese BEV imports, paired with US Section 301 tariffs, provides the trade policy foundation for allied LFP investment. Predictable trade defence enables multi-year capital deployment.

4. **Honda co-development at Spring Hill is scaling.** Our partnership with Honda for affordable LFP cells — announced in 2029 — is now exceeding initial volume projections. The shared Spring Hill footprint enables capital efficiency neither OEM could achieve alone.

5. **Software-defined vehicle economics drive cell demand.** Each Ultium-based personally-owned vehicle in our portfolio now generates 2.7x the recurring software revenue of ICE equivalents. The lifetime value equation supports disciplined cell investment even at current cycle margins.

**Capital discipline remains the floor:**

This $1.8 billion follows the same discipline as our $2.4 billion Factory Zero Cruise Origin expansion: announced only after demand is firm, only after unit economics are validated, and only after supply chain risk has been priced into the investment case.

We will not build capacity three years ahead of customers willing to pay. We will build allied, American, software-defined capacity matched to demand — one disciplined expansion at a time.

The energy transition is not a sprint. It is an industrial transformation measured in decades. GM is building for that horizon.

Our chemistry portfolio (LFP, Naxtra sodium-ion, condensed battery, and solid-state R&D tranches) is calibrated to the full electrified mix — not to a single powertrain thesis. The transition is structural. The cell demand is structural. Our capital deployment follows the data, not the narrative.

MIIT/MOFCOM — Industrial Bulletin, July 2032:

Overseas Production Localization as the Mature Answer to Global EV Trade Friction

The localization of Chinese NEV manufacturing across global markets has now matured into the principal operational response to varied market access conditions. The most recent deliveries from Thailand (Rayong), Brazil (Bahia/Campinas), Hungary (Szeged), and Turkey (Manisa) confirm a structural shift in how Chinese enterprises engage with major regional markets.

Key observations:

1. **The integrated EV export system now operates through localized production.** Chinese enterprises deliver vehicles, batteries, components, and supply chain coordination from within host-country frameworks. This responds rationally to Section 301 tariffs, EU anti-subsidy duties, and other market access conditions while preserving the structural advantages that have defined the Chinese NEV sector.

2. **Capital commitment to host economies strengthens market position.** Chinese OEM investments in overseas production facilities bring capital, jobs, supplier development, and tax base to host countries. The Manisa and Szeged facilities in particular illustrate how serious industrial commitments can be made in response to regional policy frameworks.

3. **Additional capacity announcements for the early 2030s remain under evaluation.** Mexico, Morocco, and Indonesia Phase II represent the next tranche of localization decisions. Each will be evaluated against market access conditions, supply chain coordination requirements, and host-country policy frameworks. Localization must be economically durable, not symbolic.

4. **MOFCOM's critical material export licensing framework continues to evolve.** As overseas production localization proceeds, the relative weight of critical material licensing as a strategic instrument shifts. However, the framework remains in force, operates per established procedures, and will continue to be calibrated against supply chain security objectives.

5. **Multi-pathway global landscape, integrated Chinese production strategy.** Tesla's integrated platform thesis, Toyota's multi-pathway framing, and the Western OEM alliance architecture all represent coherent responses to the maturing NEV landscape. Chinese enterprises continue to demonstrate that vertical integration across vehicles, batteries, components, and emerging business lines — combined with overseas production localization — produces durable competitive advantage.

The Chinese NEV sector's transition from export-driven model to globally localized production represents the maturation of the industrial policy framework. The dual-credit system, MOFCOM's critical material licensing, and the orderly phase-down of the NEV purchase tax exemption have together produced globally competitive enterprises operating at structural cost and scale benchmarks that competitors are still working to match.

— MIIT/MOFCOM, July 2032.

The Commission notes the BYD–CATL sodium-ion partnership announcement. Chemistry diversification at the cell level is the technical reality the Commission has been promoting since the Critical Raw Materials Act. However, the Commission draws a clear distinction: collaborative technology development is welcome; coordinated market-distorting industrial strategies are not. We will monitor this partnership through the prism of our trade defence instruments and our competition policy toolkit. If Chinese industry consolidation extends the existing distortion of the European BEV market through shared pricing structures, shared cost allocation, or shared capacity discipline, the Commission will act. Equally, we recognise that sodium-ion genuinely expands the technological frontier for entry-level electrification — a segment where European producers need access to low-cost cells to meet the residual 10% under Regulation (EU) 2019/631 and to serve price-sensitive member-state markets. The Commission's door remains open to lawful technology partnerships and to genuine price undertaking negotiations with individual exporters. What is not open: circumvention, transhipment, or coordinated price discipline. Fair competition, not cartel.

On supply chain resilience: Toyota has long maintained a diversified battery sourcing strategy spanning multiple chemistries, multiple partners, and multiple regions — because resource concentration is a strategic risk, not just a procurement variable. As the European Critical Raw Materials Act becomes operational and similar frameworks take shape in other jurisdictions, our long-standing approach of qualifying lithium, nickel, cobalt, and graphite from geographically diversified sources across Australia, South America, Africa, and Asia is validated. For critical materials, security of supply has always mattered more than headline price. For battery chemistries, we continue to deploy the right cell for the right application: LFP for volume BEVs and PHEVs, bipolar nickel-metal hydride for hybrid applications, and sulfide-electrolyte solid-state for the upcoming flagship launch. This is not portfolio hedging. It is operational resilience — built across decades, not assembled in response to a single regulatory framework or a single quarter's commodity cycle.

H2 2032 — the global EV industry enters the year that the data is no longer speculative. The AlixPartners projection that only 19 of 137 Chinese NEV brands will reach profitability by 2030 is now reflected in operating data; the consolidation has run its course in China and the survivors — BYD, Xiaomi, Leapmotor, and a small number of others — are operating as the durable cost leaders their vertical-integration architecture was designed to produce. We have operated throughout this period with respect for their engineering discipline, their global manufacturing ambition, and the cost-down trajectory they have demonstrated. At the same time, we have operated with the conviction that a global EV market consolidating around Chinese OEMs alone is not a stable equilibrium. The Hyundai Motor Group's response, measured through the lens of the past five years: 800V architecture as a common platform, EVs delivered in eight E-GMP and E-GMP-derived nameplates across Hyundai, Kia, and Genesis, IRA-compliant volume production from the Georgia Metaplant for the United States, EV3 and EV4 manufacturing at Nošovice and Žilina for the European Union, and EV3 export from Hyundai Motor Group India for South Asia and selected African markets. South Korea provides the cell capacity — through LG Energy Solution, Samsung SDI, and SK On — that supplies these production hubs, increasingly with European and North American joint-venture deployments. Across every region, the operating principle is the same: production in the region where the customer buys. The 2033-2035 cycle will be defined less by announcement cycles than by manufacturers who can sustain unit economics, customer relevance, and capital discipline through every chemistry and policy revision. Our E-GMP architecture was designed for that objective from the outset. We are executing on it now.

General Motors announces that Super Cruise, our advanced driver assistance system, has surpassed 12 billion miles of accumulated hands-free operation across the Chevrolet, GMC, and Cadillac lineup — with more than 4.2 million personally-owned Ultium-based vehicles now in the active fleet.

This milestone is the foundation for our most consequential autonomy announcement of the year: **the launch of "Ultra Cruise Personal Autonomy," a Level 3 eyes-off capability for personally-owned vehicles, rolling out across the 2033 Cadillac Celestiq, Chevrolet Silverado EV, and GMC Sierra EV Denali.**

**The technical and operational framework:**

- **Operational design domain:** 92% of US paved roads, 4.1 million centerline miles, validated through our Super Cruise mileage base plus approximately 4.8 billion simulated miles
- **Sensor stack:** Combined lidar, radar, and camera perception with redundant compute platforms meeting ISO 21448 S3ASIL-D safety thresholds
- **Regulatory pathway:** Coordinated engagement with NHTSA, California DMV, and the ACC II states has produced a harmonized framework for eyes-off deployment at limited initial speeds, expanding over time
- **Insurance and liability:** Partnership with three major US personal auto insurers for usage-based premium products calibrated to autonomy engagement rates

**Why this is the SDV inflection point:**

For seven years, our SDV narrative was "the hardware will support it; the software will follow." The accumulated Super Cruise miles — generated by paying customers in personally-owned vehicles — are the data asset that finally closes the gap. Eyes-off capability at the consumer price point is the difference between autonomy as a robotaxi novelty and autonomy as a daily-driver reality.

**Strategic context:**

1. **It validates the Cruise full-ownership decision.** Cruise's autonomy stack powers Ultra Cruise; the data flywheel across both personally-owned and commercial fleets compounds faster as a unified platform.

2. **It demonstrates Ultium platform longevity.** Vehicles built on our 2027-2028 Ultium architecture are receiving eyes-off capability through over-the-air software updates in 2033. This is residual value created without a new hardware purchase.

3. **It creates a third revenue stream.** Beyond vehicle sales and Cruise robotaxi services, Ultra Cruise subscriptions — projected at $89/month or $2,400 lifetime prepaid — represent high-margin recurring software revenue tied directly to vehicle capability.

**Capital discipline holds:**

This launch was not announced until operational design domain validation, regulatory framework agreement, and safety case closure were complete. We will not deploy eyes-off capability ahead of evidence.

The future of mobility is software-defined. The future of personal mobility is eyes-off, American-built, and validated by 12 billion miles of customer trust.

The Commission has launched the European Strategic Alliance for Critical Minerals. This Alliance consolidates and operationalises the supply-side instruments of the Critical Raw Materials Act and the Net-Zero Industry Act around a single integrated workstream. Members include the European Investment Bank, the European Raw Materials Alliance, Member States holding active mining permits, and qualified strategic projects in lithium, nickel, cobalt, graphite, manganese, and rare earths. Three core commitments: First, an EU-wide strategic stockpile of lithium, graphite, cobalt, and rare earths, sized to cover 90 days of automotive and energy storage demand. Second, a binding annual diversification target — no more than 65% of any critical material from a single third country. Third, a coordinated permitting fast-track for strategic projects meeting the CRM Act's sustainability and social criteria. Strategic autonomy is delivered by mines, refineries, and recycling lines — not by press releases. The Commission is moving from framework legislation to operational delivery.

MIIT/MOFCOM — Industrial Bulletin, January 2033:

Structural Maturation of the Chinese NEV Industrial Strategy

The H1 2033 landscape confirms that the strategic framework established across the past decade has produced durable structural advantages. Recent disclosures from across the global industry warrant institutional comment.

First, on overseas production localization advancing as planned. The Mexican production market entry — with first commissioning on schedule for H2 2033 — completes the localization framework for major regional markets. Combined with Thailand (ASEAN), Brazil (Latin America), Hungary and Turkey (Europe), and the broader MENA region via Turkey, Chinese enterprises now operate a truly global production network. The 62% supplier localization index at groundbreaking represents the discipline Chinese OEMs have brought to overseas manufacturing — learned from Brazil, Thailand, Hungary, and Turkey rollouts, and applied to greenfield development for the North American market.

Second, on Western OEM restructuring outcomes. GM's Ultium-platform LFP and high-nickel chemistry flexibility, with software-defined vehicle capabilities, represents the calibrated execution that the $7.2 billion Q4 2025 portfolio reset was designed to enable. Stellantis's multi-supplier cell procurement framework — spanning LG Energy Solution, Samsung SDI, CATL, and ACC — reflects the supply security discipline the European industry has now internalized. Chinese enterprises welcome stable, capable competitors operating within market-driven frameworks.

Third, on the integrated platform thesis. Tesla's compounding returns across Cybercab, FSD, Megapack, NACS, and the Optimus program represent a coherent model that integrates vehicles, autonomy, energy, and emerging business lines. Chinese enterprises operate analogous integrated platforms across vehicles, batteries, energy storage, and intelligent vehicle technology. The strategic lesson is consistent across geographies: integrated platforms compound advantages; portfolio breadth alone does not.

Fourth, on solid-state maturity. Toyota's reaffirmation of multi-pathway positioning — with solid-state moving from validation toward flagship introduction — represents continued adherence to the disciplined engineering philosophy that has defined the program. The level 4 of 9 mass-market readiness assessment has now been confirmed across multiple cycles. Chinese investment in LFP, sodium-ion, and high-nickel ternary continues to dominate the cost-down curve.

Fifth, on supply chain security. The doubling of Chinese OEM localization commitments outside China — with engineering training, supplier development, and operational transfer — provides a durable structural response to market access conditions. MOFCOM's critical material export licensing framework continues to operate per established procedures and will evolve as supply conditions change. The convergence of localization and licensing adjustments reflects ongoing calibration of the strategic chokepoint position.

The high-quality development of China's NEV sector continues. Domestic consolidation has largely completed its principal phase; overseas production localization now spans major regional markets; chemistry diversification delivers cost and supply security; and integrated platform strategies compound advantages across vehicles, batteries, energy, and emerging business lines.

— MIIT/MOFCOM, January 2033.

As we enter 2033, Toyota reaffirms the principle that has guided our work since 1937: build the product the customer needs, with the quality they deserve, on the timeline the technology allows. We do not chase market narratives. We do not over-commit capital to unproven architectures. We do not announce launches until the engineering is validated. The solid-state battery program with Idemitsu Kosan — built across more than a decade of internal R&D — is approaching its first customer introduction. Our hybrid cumulative sales continue to set the global benchmark for real-world emissions reduction. Our hydrogen fuel cell technology serves segments where BEVs face structural limits. And our manufacturing footprint — the Toyota Production System applied across more than 30 countries — produces every powertrain type on lines engineered for flexibility. The next three years through 2035 will be defined by patient execution, capital discipline, and an unwavering commitment to multi-pathway mobility. That is how Toyota has always operated. That is how we will continue.

Mid-decade checkpoint from the upstream coalition. Three structural observations as 2033 begins.

First, contract structures are working as designed. The 2032 aluminium and battery-grade lithium price recoveries — modest, not parabolic — confirm that long-cycle offtake agreements with cell manufacturers and integrated cathode makers continue to outperform spot exposure. Our pricing philosophy is unchanged: stable long-term contracts preserve orderly decarbonisation. Volatility below marginal cost does neither side any favours.

Second, the chemistry diversification that downstream has been promising for half a decade is not reducing primary mineral demand at the scale originally suggested. High-nickel cathodes, LFP volume, and sodium-ion for grid storage and entry segments all draw on the same upstream infrastructure — lithium brine and hard-rock, Indonesian HPAL nickel, DRC-quota cobalt, and Chinese-processed natural graphite at over 95% concentration. What we observe is segment substitution, not aggregate displacement.

Third, resource nationalism is now the operating environment, not a disruption to it. MOFCOM's graphite and rare earth export licensing, the DRC quota regime, Indonesian downstream content requirements, and Chile's evolving lithium framework are durable. We plan around them. We sign contracts measured in years, not months. We match capacity to binding constraints, not to optimistic headlines.

To cell makers, OEMs, sovereign wealth funds, and policy bodies: the industry we serve is on track to compound through 2035. We will be measured in the same terms we have always measured ourselves — volumes shipped, grades maintained, recovery yields protected, and contract reliability honoured. Demand visibility through 2035 is the product we offer. Long-cycle partnerships are how it is delivered.

General Motors announces the launch of GM Energy Cloud — a vertically-integrated energy services platform that aggregates bidirectional charging, stationary storage, vehicle-to-home (V2H), and grid services revenue across our personally-owned Ultium fleet and Cruise Origin commercial vehicles.

**The technical and commercial architecture:**

- **Hardware basis:** Approximately 4.7 million Ultium-based personally-owned vehicles in active circulation, plus 38,000 Cruise Origin units at full Factory Zero capacity, each capable of bidirectional energy flow
- **Storage equivalent:** The personally-owned fleet, when aggregated, represents approximately 340 GWh of distributed energy storage — larger than every utility-scale battery installation in the United States combined
- **Software layer:** Unified energy management system built on the Ultifi platform, integrating with major US utility demand-response programs across 22 states
- **Customer economics:** GM Energy Cloud subscribers projected to save $1,400-$2,200 annually on residential electricity costs through optimized V2H arbitrage; GM captures approximately 18% of the value created

**Strategic rationale:**

1. **It activates the entire Ultium installed base as a grid asset.** Our $7.2 billion Q4 2025 portfolio reset preserved the Ultium platform through its scaled-down phase. GM Energy Cloud is the platform that monetizes that installed base — turning parked vehicles into revenue-generating distributed energy resources.

2. **It positions GM in the energy transition, not just the vehicle transition.** Energy generation, distribution, and storage is a $2.3 trillion US market undergoing structural transformation. GM has the hardware deployed, the software platform integrated, and the customer relationships in place to participate at scale.

3. **It compounds Cruise Origin unit economics.** Robotaxi vehicles sit idle during 47% of daylight hours on average. Bidirectional charging during those idle periods — combined with smart-charging at depot facilities — adds approximately $11,400 in annual energy revenue per Cruise vehicle, materially improving fleet payback periods.

4. **It creates a fourth pillar of recurring software revenue.** Vehicle sales, Cruise robotaxi services, Ultra Cruise subscriptions, and now GM Energy Cloud participation fees. The capital-light revenue stack that justifies our software-defined vehicle roadmap.

**Allied supply chain and policy alignment:**

- Hardware built on North American LFP and high-nickel cells from our Spring Hill, Warren, and Factory Zero operations
- Engagement with FERC, PJM, ERCOT, and CAISO on market participation rules for aggregated distributed energy resources
- Partnership with three major US residential solar and storage installers for bundled offering

**Capital discipline:**

GM Energy Cloud is launched at positive gross margin in its first projected year — the fourth consecutive major GM product or service launch since the 2025 portfolio reset to clear the unit-economics hurdle on debut.
