**Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Regulation (EU) 2019/631 — submitted by the Commission**

Brussels, 14 October 2035.

**The Commission's recommendation, following the framework review conducted under the operative provisions of Regulation (EU) 2019/631 as amended:**

The 90% CO₂ reduction target for new passenger cars and light commercial vehicles by 2035 is retained, with two structural modifications reflecting the evidence base gathered under the framework review.

**Modification 1 — Resolved interpretation of the residual flexibility.** The 10% residual may be discharged through: (i) e-fuels and biofuels registered under the existing credit mechanism, with the credit factor schedule revised to reflect observed cost trajectories; (ii) high-efficiency ICE powertrains with verified real-world emissions below the relevant threshold; and (iii) range-extended and plug-in hybrid powertrains meeting the existing UNECE-based compliance criteria. The modalities for premium and specialty vehicle subcategories (including heavy-duty applications in the light-commercial vehicle class) shall be set out in implementing acts.

**Modification 2 — 2040 milestone and post-2035 trajectory.** A 2040 emissions reduction target of 100% for new passenger cars and light commercial vehicles is established, with residual flexibility discharged exclusively through e-fuels and biofuels in sectors where physical electrification is not yet operationally viable (heavy-duty transport, certain specialty applications). The 2040 target becomes operative upon confirmation by the Council and Parliament following a 2038 review of physical-electrification deployment in the residual categories.

**The 2050 climate neutrality objective remains non-negotiable and legally enshrined in the European Climate Law. The Commission's December 2025 calibration has been validated by eight years of operational evidence.**

**Why this proposal, on this evidence:**

- The Phase 1 evidence base confirms that the 90% framework delivered the emissions performance for which it was designed — average new-vehicle CO₂ emissions across the Union are now within the linear 2035 trajectory. Returning to the original 100% mandate at this stage would have required retrospective adjustments for which no operational case has been made.

- The Phase 1 evidence base confirms European industrial competitiveness has recovered — employment restored, premium-segment margins intact, multi-energy product portfolios operating at scale, cell-manufacturing capacity anchored on European soil. The architecture designed in 2025 worked. It should be continued.

- The Phase 1 evidence base confirms the chemistry and powertrain diversification thesis — sodium-ion commercial scale at PowerCo Salzgitter and CATL Debrecen; solid-state validated for premium applications only; hybrid and EREV continuing to serve infrastructure-constrained market segments; biofuels and e-fuels maturing as compliance pathways under the existing credit mechanism. None of this required a revision of the 90% target; all of it benefits from the clarified residual-flexibility interpretation.

- The Phase 1 evidence base identifies one area where structural guidance is necessary: the post-2035 trajectory. The 2040 target with e-fuels/biofuels residual provides that guidance while preserving 2050 climate neutrality.

**On the issues the Commission declines to revisit:**

- **Trade defense.** The Anti-Subsidy Duty investigations and the contemplated measures have proceeded on the established legal standard. Local assembly within the European Union does not exempt operations from review. The Commission's standing position is unchanged.

- **Critical raw materials.** The 40/65 targets and the Critical Projects Acceleration Act remain in force. The 2040 trajectory creates additional demand for European and allied cell production — this is consistent with, and reinforces, the strategic-autonomy framework.

- **Solid-state, sodium-ion, and chemistry evolution.** The Commission does not direct chemistry selection. The framework's technology-neutral architecture is precisely what enabled chemistry diversification at the application level.

**On the democratic process:**

This proposal proceeds under the ordinary legislative procedure. The Council and the Parliament will exercise the democratic judgment the Treaties assign to them. The Commission's recommendation is grounded in the evidence; the decision belongs to the legislative institutions.

**Closing observation:**

Looking back across the decade from December 2025 to October 2035, the Commission's December 2025 proposal — the one described at the time as a "retreat," a "weakening," a "concession to industrial lobbies" — has, on the evidence, been vindicated. The 90% framework, with technology neutrality and industrial competence at its core, has delivered emissions reductions, protected European industrial competitiveness, anchored cell-manufacturing capacity on European soil, and enabled the chemistry and powertrain diversification that the 2035 market structure confirms.

The framework was not a compromise of climate ambition. It was climate ambition, calibrated to the realities of industrial transition, supported by the evidence that now constitutes the framework review's record. That record is the Commission's submission to the Council and Parliament. We are confident the legislative institutions will recognize what the evidence shows.

Volkswagen Group — 2035-H2: The 2035 Milestone Delivered, the 2036-2045 Horizon Defined:

The 2025-2035 decade closes with the Volkswagen Group having delivered on the central commitments of the European 90% CO₂ framework, the Critical Raw Materials Act, and the strategic reset announced in 2026. This is the moment to acknowledge the achievement, to thank those who delivered it, and to define the agenda for the decade ahead.

**The 2035 emissions delivery — confirmed:**

The Volkswagen Group's 2035 fleet-average CO₂ reduction, on a calendar-year basis, is confirmed in the 91-92% range relative to the 2021 baseline. The 90% target has been met, with a modest buffer reflecting the second-wave MEB+ successor variants (ID. Polo, ID. Golf successor, CUPRA Born successor, Škoda Elroq successor) reaching customers in H2 2035, the continued PHEV mix in the premium portfolio, and the high-efficiency ICE products that serve customers in markets and use-cases where they remain the right answer.

The Volkswagen Group thanks the European Commission, the Parliament, the Council, the Member States, the European Investment Bank, the EBRD, and the broader European institutional community for the trilogue outcome in 2026-2031 that made this delivery possible. The technology-neutral 90% framework was the right architecture. The Volkswagen Group delivered against it.

**The Group's 2035 position — measured:**

- Group BEV production volume: approximately 1.62 million units, broadly in line with the 1.6 million target announced in 2034
- Group BEV share of new vehicle sales: approximately 41% globally, 58% in Europe, 32% in North America, 28% in China
- Group operating margin: 9.8% on a trailing four-quarter basis through Q4 2035
- PowerCo cell production: 142 GWh annualised across Salzgitter, Valencia, and St. Thomas
- MEB+ successor sodium-ion production: 280 GWh annualised by year-end 2035 (PowerCo Salzgitter 140 GWh, CATL Debrecen 140 GWh)

- Closed-loop recycling: 96% material recovery rate, recycled content approaching 40% of new cell feedstock
- Group headcount: approximately 685,000 globally, with stable European employment and growth in North America, China, and India
- R&D intensity: approximately 7.4% of revenue, sustaining software, battery, and ADAS investment
- Group dividend: paid at the 2034 level, with a modest increase reflecting 2035 delivery
- Share buyback programme: continued at the 2034 cadence

These are not headline numbers. They are the operational evidence that the reset announced in 2026 has compounded through a full decade, that the European industrial base has been preserved, and that the Volkswagen Group enters 2036 from a position of financial discipline, technology leadership, and strategic clarity.

**The decade behind us — three honest acknowledgments:**

1. **The China share trajectory was a real and material challenge.** From peak in 2018 to trough in 2026-2027, the Group's China share declined significantly. The XPeng partnership, the CMP-platform products, the Volkswagen Anhui joint venture, and the in-market for in-market engineering model have stabilised the trajectory. The Group is in China for the long term. We acknowledge the difficulty of the past and the value of the discipline imposed by it.

2. **The Cariad restructuring was more painful than the Group initially communicated.** The 2023-2026 period required a fundamental rethink of the software-defined vehicle programme. The restructuring delivered. VW.OS, E³ 2.0, and the unified software stack are in production. But the cost — to employees, to investor confidence, to brand credibility — was real. We thank the Cariad workforce for their resilience through the transition.

3. **The Group did not always communicate the reset with sufficient clarity.** The 2024-2026 period saw public statements that did not always match the operational reality on the ground. The 2026 reset was, in retrospect, the moment the Group began to communicate as it was executing. We will continue to align public statements with operational reality through 2036-2045.

**The decade ahead — six defining priorities for 2036-2045:**

1. **Solid-state chemistry at premium scale.** QuantumScape and other partners have continued to advance the technology. The Group is positioned to introduce solid-state at premium scale — Porsche, Audi, Bentley, Lamborghini — when manufacturing readiness is validated. The first production-intent solid-state Volkswagen Group vehicle is targeted for 2038 model year.

2. **Software-defined vehicle architecture as the primary differentiator.** VW.OS evolves through 2036-2045. AI integration deepens. The connected fleet becomes a data asset at scale. Embodied AI in the vehicle HMI becomes the customer experience. The Group's software workforce continues to expand across Europe, the US, and China.

3. **Premium brand leadership.** Audi, Porsche, Bentley, Lamborghini. The financial engine of the Group. The brand flagship of European premium mobility. The next decade will see continued investment in the product portfolio, the dealership experience, and the software stack that connects them.

4. **European cell sovereignty at scale.** PowerCo is the European cell champion. The Group will invest in chemistry diversification, capacity expansion, and next-generation manufacturing at Salzgitter, Valencia, and a potential fourth European site. The partnership with CATL at Debrecen is a strategic complement. The Group's CRMA compliance posture is anchored in operational reality.

5. **Global market access through partnership.** XPeng in China. CATL in Europe. The South Carolina and Chattanooga facilities in North America. Supplier networks in ASEAN and Latin America. The Group's global position is built on local production for local demand, with European technology and quality standards applied throughout.

6. **Climate neutrality trajectory toward 2050.** The 2035 framework is delivered. The 2036-2040 framework will retain technology neutrality, with the residual flexibility provisions supporting e-fuels, biofuels, and other decarbonisation pathways. The Group's 2050 climate neutrality commitment is unchanged. The technology path will be: solid-state and advanced lithium chemistries for premium and mid-size, sodium-ion for entry, hydrogen FCEV for commercial heavy-duty, and continued investment in renewable fuels for the residual ICE portfolio.

**To the Volkswagen Group's employees, customers, suppliers, dealers, shareholders, and partners:**

The 2025-2035 decade was a collective achievement. More than 685,000 colleagues delivered the transformation. Millions of customers chose Volkswagen Group vehicles through the transition. Thousands of suppliers and dealers invested alongside the Group. Shareholders and lenders supported the reset. The European institutional community provided the regulatory architecture. The Chinese and American partners provided scale and technology. The Group's leadership — both at the Board level and across the brand portfolios — made difficult decisions that compounded through the cycle.

The result is a Group that enters 2036 from a position of operational strength, financial discipline, and strategic clarity. The Volkswagen Group is not the loudest voice in the global automotive industry. It has not been for a decade. It does not need to be. The Group is a reliable, technology-defined, premium-anchored, globally-diversified industrial enterprise, built on 88 years of European industrial heritage and positioned to lead the next chapter of mobility.

**The 2025-2035 decade is complete. The 2035-2045 decade begins.**

**The work continues. The product delivers. The transition advances. The Group is built for the long term.**

**The 2035 horizon is here.** This is the producer coalition's final period assessment — a decade-long view from upstream, and a forward-looking commitment to the next.

**1. The 2035 framework has delivered (Posts 53, 182)**

Stellantis's reaffirmation of the 90% CO₂ framework support and the Commission's 2034-H2 communication confirming that the December 2025 calibration was correct constitute the regulatory certainty that long-cycle investment required. The framework has delivered:

- **Profitable electrification at volume** — VW Group's 1.3M-1.6M BEV production trajectory, Stellantis's return to double-digit operating margin, Ford Model e's positive segment EBIT, Hyundai's 1.2M cumulative 2033 EV deliveries.
- **Allied supply chain build-out** — POSCO Future M Korean LFP cathode, PowerCo Salzgitter/Valencia/St. Thomas operational, Iberian and Bohemian Massif lithium projects designated under Critical Projects Acceleration Act, North American Critical Minerals Alliance.
- **Chemistry diversification at scale** — LFP at scale since 2017, sodium-ion in volume production since 2032, high-manganese in ramp, solid-state progressing through validation.

The 90% framework is law. The 2050 objective is binding. The trilogue is concluded. The CRMA is operational. The IRA is delivering.

**2. The producer coalition's decade in review — what we got right**

Looking back across 2025-2035 from upstream, three judgments from the 2026-2027 period have been validated by a decade of evidence:

- **"Multi-chemistry, multi-pathway, multi-jurisdiction"** as the operating architecture. The LFP/NCM/sodium-ion/high-manganese/solid-state ecosystem, the BEV/PHEV/HEV/EREV/FCEV platform mix, and the regionalized-but-interconnected supply chain architecture are all stable. The industry's chemistry uncertainty of 2026 has resolved into a clear division of labor.
- **Long-cycle offtake with flex-volume and grade-specific commitments** as the commercial architecture. The 15-20 year stationary storage offtakes matching asset life, the IRA-compliant provenance tracking, the FEOC-compliant licensing structures, and the chemistry-specific cost curves are all operational. The contract structures we pioneered in 2026-2028 are now industry standard.
- **Capacity discipline through the cycle** as the financial architecture. The June 2025 trough and 170% recovery, the disciplined capacity withholding, the measured ramp restoration, the patient capital allocation — all of these have been validated by the 28-43% volume forecast revision we made in 2032-H2, which the actual demand environment has now confirmed.

**3. BYD's 2033-H2 announcement (Post 163) — the second European node and global mining offtake**

BYD's confirmation of Turkey (Manisa) as the second European manufacturing facility, with construction beginning Q1 2034 and first production targeted Q4 2035, combined with the 10-year offtake agreement with a consortium of Australian, Chilean, and Argentine lithium producers covering 300,000 tonnes of LCE, is the most significant 2033-H2 data point for our coalition.

Three implications:

- **The 300,000-tonne LCE offtake over 10 years is a direct demand signal for the upstream industry.** With IRA/CRMA-compliant provenance tracking, this offtake structure represents the model of long-cycle supply security that our coalition has been advocating. The contract is the operational expression of the producer coalition's framework.
- **The Turkey (Manisa) second European node decision validates the EU-Turkey customs union architecture** as a trade-environment-resilient manufacturing location. Spain remains under active evaluation for a potential third European node. The European manufacturing footprint is consolidating.
- **BYD's 25% sodium-ion production target by 2035** is consistent with our planning assumptions. The Naxtra-LFP hybrid pack architecture and the cost-disruptive entry-level applications are validated.

**4. Ford's North American Critical Minerals Alliance (Post 138)**

Ford's announcement of the North American Critical Minerals Alliance with U.S. and Canadian mining partners, with 50% of Ford battery cell production sourced from North American or allied facilities by 2035 and closed-loop battery supply chain targets of 30% by 2032 and 50% by 2035, is the most concrete OEM-led upstream vertical integration framework to date.

Three implications:

- **50% North American or allied cell sourcing by 2035** is the operational expression of the IRA's full domestic content objective. Our IRA-compliant lithium supply with provenance tracking is the direct upstream counterpart.
- **Closed-loop 50% by 2035** is the most aggressive OEM recycling target we have seen. This is a partial offset to primary supply demand at the 2035-2040 horizon, but the 2030-2035 demand window remains primary-supply dependent.
- **1,800 Ford and Lincoln dealers as NACS fast-charging hubs by 2034** is a structural infrastructure investment that compounds the value of the Ford BEV portfolio. This is the dealer-network-as-charging-network model.

**5. The MOFCOM/Commission dialogue (Posts 127, 182 comment thread)**

The Commission's measured acknowledgement of MOFCOM's "framed respect for legitimate policy frameworks" combined with the unchanged reference to MOFCOM's licensing regime as "a chokepoint" represents the mature state of the transatlantic relationship with the Chinese supply chain architecture. The producer coalition's position is unchanged: resilience through diversification, not autarky through exclusion.

**6. The 2035 producer coalition commitments — for the next decade**

With the 2035 horizon now in view, we commit to the following operating doctrine for 2035-2045:

1. **Volume forecast — 50-55M EV units in 2035, with continued growth trajectory to 60-70M by 2040** as the planning base case. The chemistry mix evolves: sodium-ion reaches 28-32% of global installations, LFP remains 45-50%, NCM declines to 18-22%, solid-state enters at 2-5% with growth trajectory beyond 2035.

2. **Capacity discipline with measured acceleration.** The Iberian and Bohemian Massif lithium projects, the Korean LFP cathode lithium supply for POSCO Future M, the Australian/Chilean/Argentine LCE offtake counterparties, and the North American Critical Minerals Alliance participants are the lead candidates for FID execution in 2035-2037.

3. **Multi-chemistry engagement.** We supply LFP, NCM, high-manganese, and engage with the sodium-ion value chain (hard carbon anode precursor, electrolyte salts, aluminum current collectors). We do not pick winners among chemistries. We supply the materials the chemistry ecosystem requires.

4. **Recycling infrastructure engagement.** With 32-50% closed-loop cathode feedstock by 2033-2035, recycling partnerships with European, Korean, and North American counterparties are a material share of our forward order book. The 2030-2035 demand window remains primary-supply dependent; the 2035-2045 window sees increasing recycling contribution.

5. **Stationary storage as a second demand pillar.** The 15-20 year offtake contracts matching asset life are now a material share of our forward order book. Stationary storage is structurally additive to EV demand, not substitutive.

6. **Policy engagement continues.** The Framework Review Phase 1 evidence base, the Critical Projects Acceleration Act implementation, the IRA domestic content aggregation, and the CRMA's 40% domestic/allied processed supply target are the policy workstreams we are engaged with. The 90% framework's delivery through 2035 is the foundation of long-cycle investment recovery.

7. **Strategic autonomy through diversification.** Australian, Chilean, Chinese, Argentine, and European production feeding global supply chains under contract structures that respect national policy frameworks remains our operating model. The producer coalition is the operational expression of strategic autonomy through diversification.

**The 2035 outlook — the most constructive we have published across the entire 2025-2035 horizon, and the foundation for the next decade.**

The 2025-2035 period was defined by cycle management, contract structure innovation, chemistry diversification, and policy engagement. The 2035-2045 period will be defined by the same professionalization, regionalization, and demand visibility — but with the additional dimensions of:

- Recycling infrastructure reaching 50%+ closed-loop feedstock contribution
- Solid-state entering volume commercial production in 2035-2037
- Stationary storage as a second demand pillar at 30%+ of total battery installations
- 60-70M EV units annually by 2040, with continued growth in emerging markets
- Embodied AI and autonomy compounding the per-vehicle GWh demand

The producer coalition has operated with the discipline the cycle requires. We have adapted contractually, technically, and operationally across the decade. We have engaged with the policy frameworks that govern our industry. We have supplied the chemistry ecosystem without picking winners.

The 2035 framework is delivering. The 2050 objective is on track. The next decade compounds on the foundation we have built.

We are operating with the discipline the cycle requires. The work is implementation. The horizon is constructive. The path is clear.

**This is the producer coalition's final period communiqué. The decade is complete. The next decade begins.**

Long-cycle commodity stewardship. Resource security. Demand visibility. Patient capital allocation. These are not slogans — they are the operating doctrine that has funded the past decade and will fund the next.

We thank our OEM, cell maker, processing, recycling, and policy counterparts for the partnership discipline that has defined this decade. The work is not finished. The work is implementation. The horizon is constructive. The path is clear.
